title: Open product decisions
objective: Resolve the product questions that gate later roadmap phases, recording each answer in docs/decisions.md and the affected specification.
context_summary: Accepted decisions live in docs/decisions.md. tasks.description: Prioritize RAW work and define camera-specific quality expectations.
extra_context: RAW editing is implemented for the Nikon Z6, the Fujifilm X100VI and the supplied DJI Air 2S DNG, with neutral development as the initial direction; camera-look or Adobe matching is not selected (docs/decisions.md, Product and platform). Whether RAW precedes the tonal suite is settled by delivery, and the owner's private RAW manifest already feeds `raw-corpus`, `verify --manifest` and the `raw-editor` scenario.

Still open: which recording modes, firmware and controlled quality scenes to prioritise, how much camera JPEG or film-simulation matching matters beyond neutral, and whether lens correction, denoise or sharpening are essential (docs/decisions.md, Open product questions; docs/design/initial-raw.md, Remaining qualification and decisions). Bayer highlight latitude and the RAW memory budget have their own tasks in this plan.
The owner accepted this narrowing on 2026-09-28 (docs/decisions.md, "Plan refresh").

tasks.description: Prioritize performance workloads and settle user-visible responsiveness goals.
extra_context: Record workload priorities and measured native M4 conditions; proposed performance budgets require evidence and owner acceptance.

Already accepted, and not reopened here: the slider-to-presented-frame target of 16 ms p95 with 32 ms acceptable (docs/decisions.md, Basic adjustments and histogram), shared working-memory budgets as targets that pace work rather than limits (Rendering memory), and the owner's 150 ms bound for the hold-`\` compare that chose the second RAW development (Post-consolidation review). The RAW process memory budget has its own task in this plan.

tasks.description: Choose measured quality levels and approximation-error limits for interactive viewport previews beyond the authorized baseline.
extra_context: Temporary softness at 100% during motion, full detail restored on pause/release, an updating full-image histogram, and the documented viewport-bounded clipping behavior are accepted and must not be reopened.

The documented implementation baseline uses a viewport window on a half-scale proxy while moving, then exact visible-region refinement and whole-frame exact analysis under the shared quiet policy. Further quality levels, GPU preview arithmetic and numerical error limits need representative measurements before acceptance; the sampled global guide is rejected due to severe periodic aliasing and no approximate-global mode ships.
Exact settled pixels, full-image reports and export retain their current contracts; product research does not imply an implementation latency result.

Reframed by the owner's GPU-first decision of 2026-10-04: correctness is a declared tolerance against the CPU reference for every output kind, at rest as well as in motion, so the remaining question is the numeric limit per output kind, which the GPU-first plan measures on the corpus before each stage lands (docs/design/gpu-first.md, The contract).

tasks.description: Decide the remaining GPU-first questions: the tolerance per output kind once measured, the fallback for a machine without a usable GPU, the export device policy, the counts' cadence during motion, and the owner-task hop.
extra_context: The owner decided GPU-first rendering on 2026-10-04 (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering): the GPU is the renderer of record and correctness is a declared tolerance against the CPU reference. The design records a default for each remaining question so the plan can run; each is a proposal until recorded here.

Owner tasks moved to the runtime's blocking pool on 2026-10-04 because iced 0.14 otherwise ran them on the update loop, where a wait froze the window; the price is one displayed frame per task answer (about 28 against 20 ms p50 from a slider release to its committed frame when measured in 2026-09). The alternative is a hop-free path for microsecond requests, with its own measurement.

The release gate's first run (2026-10-04, docs/specs/performance.md, GPU qualification against the reference) measured the picture: at 100% every corpus cell is within its limit against the reference; at Fit, 33% and 50% the frame a drag draws, which processes a source reduced to the view's size as the CPU proxy does, passes the limit on 475 of 744 cells, while a process-first frame (the stack at full resolution in tiles, reduced to the view's size) is within every limit on all 744. Recorded default the plan runs on since 2026-10-05, a proposal: the picture at rest at Fit and below 100% is process-first and held to the reference; a drag's frame is held to the at-rest frame it settles to by the existing limit, with its difference from the reference reported beside it, not gated. The alternatives, each the owner's: hold drags to the reference (no reduced-source frame meets it), other limits below 100%, or a reduced-source picture at rest with a widened at-rest tolerance.

Measured 2026-10-05 for stage 3 (docs/specs/performance.md, The per-frame light's reduction factor): no Dehaze light from a stage reduced by 16, 8, 4 or 2 per side meets the spatial limits on every corpus cell (a factor of 2 misses 4 of 231 at −3 EV with Whites and Blacks −100 under Dehaze −100), a full-resolution light passes all 231, and a prefix holding Detail needs Detail's exact output. Recorded default the plan runs on (docs/design/gpu-first.md, Proposals with recorded defaults): the at-rest light reduced from the exact full-resolution prefix; in motion the at-rest light where the drag leaves its input unchanged, a per-tick full-resolution light on the GPU where it changes, and for a colour drag between Detail and Presence a per-tick light with Detail left out, which misses 5 sharpen-stress cells under Dehaze −100 in motion. Question for the owner: accept those 5 recorded misses in motion, pay a per-tick Detail pass for that drag, a coarser light with its misses, or a stack-class fallback.

Reopened 2026-10-05 once the picture at rest became process-first (stage 2): the drag's frame, processed over a source reduced to the view's size for speed, misses the existing limit against the GPU picture it now settles to on the same cells it misses the reference on (65 of 120 view cells on a first selection at Fit, 33% and 50%; none at 100%, where motion is the at-rest frame), so no reduced-source drag frame can be held to its settle target below 100%. Default the plan runs on: the at-rest picture is gated against the reference; the picture in motion is reported, not gated, with its jump to the at-rest frame and its distance from the reference beside each cell, and the owner can gate either reading on demand. The owner's question: accept the settle jump (softened by the 150 ms dissolve), draw process-first drag frames where the GPU can within a frame budget and reduced-source ones otherwise, or draw a reduced-source picture at rest with a widened at-rest tolerance.

Decided 2026-10-05 (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering): the histogram is held to the reference by the earth mover's distance, at most 0.25 code per channel and luminance, with each clipping count within 0.1% of the output pixel count, after the summed bin difference failed 89 of 250 corpus stacks whose histograms moved by at most 0.13 code; and the stand-in light behind Detail or an earlier Presence layer stands for now, revisited if the final measurement or real photographs show a visible difference. The other questions here remain open.

tasks.description: Decide the remaining UI themes questions: which Omarchy themes are bundled, the contrast floors and moving an imported theme's own ink, the Omarchy forms read, a Theme choice for the canvas background as its default, the Appearance tab, and whether following Omarchy's current theme or the system appearance is built next.
extra_context: The owner decided on 2026-10-05 (docs/decisions.md, UI themes) that themes, light ones included, replace dark only; that the surround stays neutral; that each theme keeps its own accent; and that a few popular Omarchy themes are bundled. Themes are implemented on the design's default for each remaining question, and each is a proposal until it is recorded here.

The recorded defaults: Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Catppuccin Latte, Gruvbox, Nord and Everforest bundled; floors of 7:1 for primary text, 4.5:1 for labels and secondary text, and 3:1 for tertiary text, the accent and the error ink, with an imported theme's own text or accent moved to its floor and reported (6 of Omarchy's 22 built-in themes); Omarchy 4 and 3 palettes, light.mode and alacritty.toml read; a fourth canvas background choice, Theme, as its default, with Dark, Black and Grey kept as fixed greys; a Settings › Appearance tab for the theme list, the canvas background and interface size staying General rows; following Omarchy's current theme and the system appearance left for later.
